synopsis: False and nuisance alarms are repeatedly identified as a leading cause of deployed proximity-system failure, with documented distrust, disabling and operator rejection; achieving an acceptable detection–false-positive balance took the manufacturer years of calibration [f5928, f6494, f10496, f10]. The strongest cited quantitative evidence remains the 2006 NIOSH report of seven days of 2004 Caterpillar 793B testing: 580 alarms over 618 reversals, with 18% false alarms and 42% nuisance alarms; the chapters report the action-worthy share slightly differently, as 40% versus 235/580 (41%) [f5173, f3010, f3011, f5174, f5175, f5176]. Validation should use real operating exposure and fleet logging, including winter 2026–2027, rather than staged targets alone; replay results remain limited to the sensors, mounting positions and scenarios actually recorded [f6656, f11336, f728, f95]. Published off-road hourly acceptance limits and standard statistical sample sizes were not found, so the program must establish separate criteria for advisory warnings, urgent warnings, speed reduction and full braking, despite MOSH's requirement for no false warnings or interventions at TRL4 [f2121, f5160, f2124, f2119]. Tuning should constrain missed or late interventions while optimizing false warnings, unnecessary brakes and productivity loss, without suppressing genuinely dangerous repeated berm alarms; false alarms in automatic braking can cause a brake slam [f136, f11522, f11306].
